standard_prerequisites.name: Essentially constant inverse systems
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the decomposition of the quotient system as a constant part plus a part whose transition maps are eventually zero, which is the form in which the hypothesis is used.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Mittag-Leffler condition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of ML for an inverse system of abelian groups
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the condition on the stabilisation of the images of the transition maps that is compared for the two systems.

core_obligations: Normal form of the hypothesis (proof lines 7989-7991): after renumbering one may write C_i = C + Z_i compatibly with the transition maps and arrange that for every i some Z_{i'} with i' at least i maps to zero in Z_i, by the cited lemma.

The case C = 0 (proof lines 7993-8003): choosing an increasing sequence of indices with Z_{n_{i+1}} -> Z_{n_i} zero, the transition map B_{n_{i+1}} -> B_{n_i} factors through A_{n_i}, so the images of A_{n_j} in A_{n_i} sit between the images of B_{n_j} and of A_{n_{j-1}}; stabilisation for the A-images is therefore equivalent to stabilisation for the B-images, and the equivalence of the Mittag-Leffler conditions follows, the author noting that this last translation is a small detail omitted.

The case C nonzero (proof lines 8005-8018): with B'_i the inverse image of C in B_i, the preceding paragraph shows that B' has ML if and only if B has ML, so one may replace B by B'; then 0 -> A_i -> B_i -> C -> 0 is exact for every i and the induced sequences 0 -> Im(A_j -> A_i) -> Im(B_j -> B_i) -> C -> 0 are short exact for j at least i, so the images stabilise simultaneously.
proof_roadmap: Put the essentially constant quotient system into its normal form.
Reduce to the case of a zero constant part and compare the two systems of images.
Reduce the general case to the zero constant part by taking inverse images.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups with essentially constant quotient, the Mittag-Leffler property holds for the sub-system if and only if it holds for the middle system (statement lines 7977-7986). The proof is a complete argument: the hypothesis is put into normal form using the cited lemma (proof lines 7989-7991), the case of a zero constant part is settled by comparing the systems of images of the two sub-diagrams (proof lines 7993-8003), and the general case is reduced to that one by replacing the middle system by the inverse image of the constant part, after which a short exact sequence of image systems finishes the argument (proof lines 8005-8018). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two image systems. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
